pages.text:
Every second the reactor works out how neutrons spread through its grid, which gives each channel's share of the power and the core's k-effective.
- Moderators (water, Heavy Water, graphite) slow neutrons so more fission in U-235.
- Control rods and fission products absorb. Water absorbs a little; Heavy Water hardly at all.
- Neutrons that leave the edge are lost; graphite or Steel Reflectors there send some back.

# Delayed neutrons
About 1% of neutrons come late. While k-effective stays under 1.01 power changes smoothly, at a reactor period you can watch. Above that the core is prompt critical and power climbs in seconds: the protection system will trip on a short period, if it's on.
# Feedback
- Hotter fuel always lowers reactivity (Doppler).
- Boiling lowers it in a water-moderated core and raises it in a graphite-moderated, water-cooled one. A positive void coefficient makes a core unstable: the GUI shows it.

# Xenon
Iodine-135 from fission decays into Xenon-135, a poison that burns away at power: as it builds after a power rise, power drifts down slowly and wants a small trim out now and then. After a big drop it builds up for a while and can delay a restart.
# Decay heat
After shutdown the core keeps giving off about 6.5% of its last power, fading over in-game hours. Keep the coolant coming.
